technical_and_design_decisions: The user stories target Spring XD (Spring eXtreme Data), a distributed runtime and toolset for data ingestion/analytics, not Spring Framework core. The Spring Framework reference is the underlying platform.

U1 (admin_ui bug): The job creation failure is a missing error handling/logging path in the admin_ui controller layer; fix by catching exceptions, logging them at ERROR level, and surfacing a meaningful error to the user. Reproduction requires both ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN, so the issue is role-agnostic and likely a server-side condition (e.g., misconfigured stream/job definition, missing container connection).

U2 (Kafka partition count): Expose an explicit `partitionCount` option on the Kafka module definition; route payloads to the targeted consumer module by encoding/hashing the partition key and using Kafka's producer partitioner.

U3 (Dynamic partition subscription): Use the Kafka AdminClient (Kafka 0.9+ API) to discover topic metadata at runtime and rebalance consumer assignments when partitions are added; integrate with the existing KafkaMessageSourceContainer lifecycle.
U4 (HDFS sync option): Add a `syncable` boolean option to the HDFS sink; when enabled, use FileSystem.hsync()/hflush() after each record write to guarantee durability at the cost of throughput.

U5 (HDFS direct filename): Add a `useTemporarySuffix` (or inverse) option to the HDFS sink; when disabled, write directly to the configured target filename without the `.tmp` suffix. Pairs naturally with U4 to support recovery from mid-write failures.

U6 (Maven/Gradle module upload): Provide Maven plugin (maven-xd-plugin) and Gradle plugin (gradle-xd-plugin) goals/tasks that call Spring XD's existing module registration REST API to upload and register module artifacts remotely.

U7 (Module versioning): Introduce a semantic version (e.g., 1.0.0) on each module. Store versions in the module metadata repository; allow side-by-side installations; let deployments select a specific version. Update the upload/install paths to handle version-aware resolution.

U8 (PHD 3.0 certification): Run the full Spring XD certification suite against a Pivotal HD 3.0 (ODP-based) Hadoop cluster; resolve any Hadoop API compatibility gaps and document supported configurations.
Testing strategy: Add unit tests (JUnit/TestNG), integration tests (Spring XD test framework with embedded containers) for each user story, and end-to-end tests for the certification deliverable.
All estimates assume a single experienced developer who is already familiar with the Spring XD codebase, uses the existing build/test infrastructure, and works on related stories sequentially.
assumptions: 1 workday = 8 hours of focused development effort (no meetings/admin overhead counted).
A single experienced Spring XD developer performs all work; no onboarding, no new hire ramp-up time.
Test infrastructure (Kafka cluster, HDFS instance, PHD 3.0 cluster) is already provisioned and available; environment provisioning is not in scope.
Spring XD continues to use the Spring Framework 6.x / Java 17+ baseline already in the platform.
U1 reproduction environment (admin_ui + container logs) is available; the bug is reproducible deterministically.
U2/U3 work targets the Kafka source module only (per U3 wording); producer-side partition routing for U2 reuses Kafka's standard partitioner and does not require custom partitioner logic.
U4 and U5 are independent switches on the HDFS sink; combined usage is supported but tested separately.
Maven and Gradle plugin support in U6 is required for both build tools; both ship as separate artifacts.
Module versioning in U7 follows semver (major.minor.patch); metadata is persisted in the existing admin DB / ZooKeeper-backed store used by Spring XD.
U8 (PHD 3.0 certification) means compatibility testing + issue fixing; deep new feature work on Hadoop integration is not implied.
Documentation updates (user/admin guides, release notes) are tracked as a single activity; no per-feature docs breakdown.
Final integration testing covers cross-story interactions (e.g., U6 + U7 upload + versioning flow).
No production deployment, training, or post-release support is included.
